Quick diagnostic from the runtime:
- Observed a sudden concentration of requests with the same prompt prefix (hot key) leading to repeated KV cache thrash on a small set of KV shards.
- Our continuous-batching pipeline is aggregating these into very large batches (max_batch_size hit) which increases per-request tail latency. When the batch holds up due to a slow GPU kernel for long sequences, everything behind it experiences HOL blocking.
- A side-effect: some requests hit an inter-op timeout path and surface as 500s.

Short mitigation (applied at 09:36 PT):
1) Reduced max_batch_size for the affected model from 64 -> 8 for the next 30m.
2) Enabled per-prefix KV sharding for that customer (split hot key to dedicated shard) — this is a lightweight config flip; should reduce cache contention.
3) Temporarily enabled request-level slow-path fallback to smaller model variant for requests exceeding 2s queue_time.
4) Started a short rate-limit on the customer API key to smooth the arrival pattern.

Early results (09:44 PT): P99 dropped to ~520ms, 5xxs down from 8% -> 1.2%. We're continuing to monitor. I'll push a small patch later today to make KV sharding more robust and add metrics for per-prefix miss-rate. Patch draft attached: patch-kv-shard-20260311.diff

Next steps:
- If stability holds for 60m, we'll craft a rollback/plan for a safe permanent config change and a postmortem.
- Create INF ticket and link to runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/kv-hotkey-mitigation

Update: the temporary mitigations are holding. 5xxs down to 0.9%, P99 ~480ms. Attached is the patch we pushed to adjust shard mapping and add a per-request sharding hint: patch-kv-shard-20260311.diff

Root cause (preliminary):
- A customer-side traffic pattern concentrated many similar prompts in a short window (hot key).
- Our KV cache mapping was using a coarse shard mapping; hot key caused thrash across a handful of GPU-local caches which then triggered large batches to form and the HOL blocking cascade.
- Coupled with no per-request sharding hint, continuous batching aggregated requests that should have been kept separate.

I'll schedule the postmortem entry (INF-4123) and attach metrics. We'll also add a new runtime metric for per-prefix queue_time and a circuit-breaker to prevent a single prefix from generating arbitrarily large batches.
